findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 15 mm is observed in the tail of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion, and the tumor extends beyond the inferior border of the duodenum. The tumor is in contact with the aorta, with an indistinct boundary, indicating invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 9. A contrast-enhancing mass is noted in the right cerebellar hemisphere, raising suspicion of brain metastasis.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU1 (invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A1 (invasion of the aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the omentum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (15 mm) and the extent of local invasion, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the tail are:
- Station 9 (left gastric artery)
- Station 11 (common hepatic artery)
- Station 12a (proper hepatic artery)
- Station 12b (common bile duct)
- Station 13 (cystic duct)
- Station 16 (splenic artery)
- Station 17 (splenic artery)
- Station 18 (pancreaticoduodenal artery)
- Station 19 (celiac artery)

The patient's metastatic lymph node station is:
- Station 9 (left gastric artery)

There is only 1 metastatic lymph node in the regional stations, so the N classification is N1a.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There is a contrast-enhancing mass in the right cerebellar hemisphere, which is a distant metastasis. Therefore, the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

The tumor is in contact with the aorta, which is a criterion for Unresectable (UR). Therefore, the resectability classification is Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T3), N classification (N1a), and M classification (M1), the overall stage is Stage IV.
